verdict.rationale: Crawl4AI's GitHub README documents its own dynamic-crawling feature that can execute JS and wait for dynamic content before extraction, which is the core of this story. The evidence never says the wait can target a specific CSS/XPath selector, so the selector-specific part is unproven. missing for 10: explicit documentation of a wait-for-selector parameter, evidence that this works through the API/server, timeout and behavior details, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can have the API wait for a specific selector to appear before returning the rendered page

citations.quote: Dynamic Crawling: Execute JS and wait for async or sync for dynamic content extraction.
